'''Elaine Surick Oran''' (born April 16, 1946) is an [[Americans|American]] physical scientist and is considered a world authority on numerical methods for large-scale simulation of physical systems.<ref name=NRL2006 /> She has pioneered computational technology to solve complex reactive flow problems, unifying concepts from science, mathematics, engineering, and computer science in a new methodology.<ref name=Rank2007 /> An incredibly diverse range of phenomena can be modeled and better understood using her techniques for numerical simulation of fluid flows, ranging from the tightly grouped movements of fish in Earth's oceans to the explosions of far-flung supernovae in space.<ref name=Spector2007 /> Her work has contributed significantly to the advancement of the engineering profession.<ref name=Spector2007 />

== Education ==
Elaine Surick is the daughter of Herman E. Surick and the stepdaughter of Doris Luterman-Surick. She is married to Daniel Oran.<ref name=DorisLutermanSurick>{{cite web|title=Obituary, Doris M. (Manstein) Luterman-Surick|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/philly/obituary.aspx?n=doris-m-luterman-surick-manstein&pid=123406269|website=Philly.com|access-date=19 October 2014}}</ref>

Elaine Surick attended school in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=Leeds2010 /> [[Bryn Mawr College]] awarded her a bachelor's degree in both physics and chemistry (1966). She then attended [[Yale University]], where she received a master's degree from the department of physics (1968) and a Ph.D. from the department of engineering and applied sciences (1972).<ref name=Spector2007 />

== U.S. Naval Research Lab ==
Elaine Oran joined the Plasma Physics Division at [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]] (NRL) in 1972.<ref name=Viterbi /><ref name=Spector2007 /> In 1978, she joined the Laboratory for Computational Physics.<ref name=Viterbi>{{cite web|title=Elaine Oran|url=http://viterbi.usc.edu/news/events/keynote/laufer/elaine-oran.htm|publisher=U.Sc. Viterbi School of Engineering|access-date=3 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141126050819/http://viterbi.usc.edu/news/events/keynote/laufer/elaine-oran.htm|archive-date=26 November 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> She worked to start the Center for Reactive Flow and Dynamical Systems, and became its head.<ref name=Leeds2010 /> In 1988, she became the senior scientist for reactive flow physics.<ref name=Viterbi /><ref name=Leeds2010 />

She has done significant theoretical and computational research on complex dynamic systems' fluid and molecular properties. Her team has created many numerical algorithms and computerized models for accurate numerical simulation of reactive flows. Because reactive flows occur in a broad range of important phenomena, Oran's work has enabled other investigators to examine and describe many previously unexplained reactive flow dynamics.<ref name=NRL2006 />

Reactive flows can involve gases, liquids, solids, or combinations thereof. As these move through space and over time, they may change chemically.<ref name=Rank2007 /> Reactive flow problems often involve multiple processes interacting simultaneously. Identifying the boundary conditions where states of matter react and how they interact is important in modeling reactive flows. Physical processes involved in reactive flows include species reactions, diffusive transport, radiative transport, convection, and wave-like properties, some or all of which may be modeled to address a particular problem. Modelling of complex reactive flows has applications in a wide variety of areas including [[aerodynamics]], [[fluid dynamics|hydrodynamics]], [[microfluidics]], [[chemical kinetics]], [[chemical process modeling]] (involving [[Advection|advective]] and [[Diffusion|diffusive]] transport processes as well as chemical kinetics) and [[combustion]]-related [[flame]] and [[detonation]] phenomena.<ref name=OranBoris>{{cite book|last1=Oran|first1=Elaine S.|author2-link=Jay P. Boris|last2=Boris|first2=Jay P.|title=Numerical simulation of reactive flow|date=2005|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge|isbn=978-0-521-02236-1|edition=2nd}}</ref>

Reactive flow modeling can be applied to solar and stellar astrophysics to study [[nova]]e, star formation, and [[cosmology]]. It can model mixing in Earth's atmosphere, rarefied gas flow during atmospheric reentry, torpedo launches in the Earth's oceans, the spread of fires in cities and forests, and the behavior of car engines and chemical lasers.<ref name=Spector2007 /><ref name=OranBoris />

Oran has applied simulation methods to various issues at the Naval Research Lab. She has helped to design biosensors, propulsion systems for rockets and jets, and space and planetary exploration vehicles. She has studied the fundamental physics of combustion processes, applying flow models to flames, detonations, and the conditions underlying the transition to denotation. Her work has supported the safe storage of hydrogen fuels and other energetic materials.<ref name=NRL2006 />

== Aerospace engineering ==
She is currently a professor at [[Texas A&M University]]. She worked at the department of [[aerospace engineering]] at the [[University of Maryland]] as a Glenn L. Martin Institute Professor of Engineering from 2013 to 2019. She continues to serve as an emeritus scientist at the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory and is an adjunct professor at the [[University of Michigan]] and a visiting professor at [[Leeds University]].<ref name=Welcome2014>{{cite news|title=Aerospace Department Welcomes New Faculty Member Elaine Oran|url=http://www.aero.umd.edu/news/news_story.php?id=7648|access-date=19 October 2014|agency=Department of Aerospace Engineering|publisher=University of Maryland}}</ref> She is also a senior visiting professor in the Institute for Advanced Study at [[Hong Kong University of Science and Technology]] and a distinguished visiting professor at [[Tsinghua University]].

== Publications ==
{{Library resources box|by=yes|viaf=19741866}}

She has published extensively in journals and has written a textbook, ''Numerical Simulation of Reactive Flow'' (1987, 2005), which is reported to be the most frequently used textbook on the topic.<ref name=NRL2006 />

== Awards and honors ==
Among many other awards and honors, Elaine Oran is an Honorary Fellow of the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]] (AIAA), "the highest distinction conferred by AIAA, … granted to preeminent individuals who have had long and highly contributory careers in aerospace, and embody the highest possible standards in aeronautics and astronautics."<ref name=Welcome2014 /> She is a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], [[National Academy of Engineering]] and an inaugural Fellow of [[The Combustion Institute]].<ref name=OranFellowAAAS /><ref name=NAEMembership /><ref name=OranFellowCI />

Other awards, honors, and honorary memberships include, but are not limited to, the following:
